page: Microsoft Azure HB368rs_v5 is a high-performance computing virtual machine instance featuring 368 dedicated x86_64 virtual central processing units powered by an Intel processor. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the platform provides 448.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.22 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include discrete graphics hardware.

For localized storage performance, the instance integrates 15,875 GB of NVMe solid-state storage alongside support for Premium Storage tiers. Inter-node communications are accelerated by Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) networking capabilities, which bypasses the standard network protocol stack to deliver low-latency message exchange across multi-node clusters.

With a focused memory allocation of 1.22 GB per core, the configuration prioritizes high thread counts and parallel execution throughput over massive per-thread memory footprint. The pairing of 368 execution cores, direct RDMA interconnects, and nearly 16 TB of local NVMe scratch disk suits tightly coupled MPI applications, computational fluid dynamics, crash simulations, weather modeling, and large distributed scientific computing jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure HB368rs_v5 is a high-performance computing virtual machine offering 368 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs driven by an Intel processor under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Designed for tightly coupled compute workloads, the system incorporates 448.0 GB of memory, resulting in an allocation ratio of 1.22 GB per vCPU. It does not feature graphical processing units. Storage capacity is substantial, providing 15,875 GB of local NVMe SSD space alongside Premium Storage capability for rapid scratch data access and high input/output throughput. Networking performance is bolstered by Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) support, which enables low-latency inter-node synchronization across high-performance compute clusters. Because of its dense core architecture and constrained per-core memory ratio, the HB368rs_v5 targets parallel execution environments where message passing efficiency and raw compute capacity take precedence over per-thread memory footprint, such as computational fluid dynamics, engineering simulations, weather forecasting, and massive scientific modeling.
